subtopics.title: Plot cosine graph and state its characteristics
subtopics.exposition: A period of 360° means that one cosine wave is completed in 360°. For y = cos θ, the values of cos θ at θ = 0°, 30°, 60°, 90°, 120°, 150°, 180°, 210°, 240°, 270°, 300°, 330°, 360° are 1; 0.87; 0.5; 0; -0.5; -0.87; -1; -0.87; -0.5; 0; 0.5; 0.87; 1. The period of y = cos θ is 360°. The amplitude of y = cos θ is 1. The maximum value of y = cos θ is 1 and the minimum value is -1. The domain of y = cos θ is [0°, 360°]. The range of y = cos θ is [-1, 1]. The x-intercepts of y = cos θ are (90°, 0) and (270°, 0). The y-intercept of y = cos θ is (0°, 1). The maximum turning points of y = cos θ are (0°, 1) and (360°, 1). The minimum turning point of y = cos θ is (180°, -1). For f(θ) = a cos θ + q, the domain is [0°, 360°]. The range of f(θ) = a cos θ + q is the same as the range of a sin θ + q, because the maximum and minimum values of a cos θ + q are the same as those of a sin θ + q. The period of y = a cos θ + q is 360°. To plot y = cos θ, use a calculator to complete a table of values of cos θ for θ from 0° to 360° in steps of 30°. Plot the points from the table and join them with a smooth curve. The y-intercept of f(θ) = a cos θ + q is found as for sine: substitute θ = 0°, so y = f(0°) = a cos 0° + q = a(1) + q = a + q. The cosine values in the table are rounded to 2 decimal places. Plot the values of θ on the x-axis and cos θ on the y-axis, choosing an appropriate scale.

subtopics.title: Sketch y = a cos θ + q
subtopics.exposition: The effect of q in y = a cos θ + q is called a vertical shift: the whole cosine graph shifts up or down by q units. The value of a affects the amplitude of the graph, that is, the height of the peaks and the depth of the troughs. For q > 0, the cosine graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units. For q < 0, the cosine graph is shifted vertically downwards by q units. For q = 0, the graph is the basic cosine graph. For a > 1, there is a vertical stretch and the amplitude increases. For a = 1, the graph is the basic cosine graph. For 0 < a < 1, the amplitude decreases. For a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis. For -1 < a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude decreases. For a < -1, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude increases. The range of f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3 is [1, 5]. The graph of f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3 has no x-intercepts. The y-intercept of f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3 is (0°, 5). The maximum turning points of f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3 are (0°, 5) and (360°, 5). The minimum turning point of f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3 is (180°, 1). To discover the effect of q, plot y = cos θ - 2, cos θ - 1, cos θ, cos θ + 1 and cos θ + 2 on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of q. To discover the effect of a, plot y = -2 cos θ, -cos θ, cos θ and 2 cos θ on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of a. To sketch a cosine graph, first examine the standard form of the equation to see from a and q how the graph is stretched, reflected or shifted. For f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3, a > 1 so the graph is stretched vertically. For f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3, q > 0 so the graph is shifted vertically upwards by 3 units. Substitute θ = 0°, 30°, ..., 360° into f(θ) = 2 cos θ + 3 to get the values 5; 4.73; 4; 3; 2; 1.27; 1; 1.27; 2; 3; 4; 4.73; 5, then plot the points and join them with a smooth curve.

subtopics.title: Find a and q from a cosine graph
subtopics.exposition: The y-intercept of f(θ) = a cos θ + q is the point (0°, a + q). For a > 0, the range of f(θ) = a cos θ + q is [-a + q, a + q]. For a < 0, the range of f(θ) = a cos θ + q is [a + q, -a + q].

subtopics.title: Compare the sine and cosine graphs
subtopics.exposition: The sine and cosine graphs look very similar: both waves move up and down along the x-axis. The distances between the peaks are the same for the sine graph and the cosine graph. The height of the peaks and the depth of the troughs are the same for the sine graph and the cosine graph. If the whole cosine graph is shifted to the right by 90°, it overlaps perfectly with the sine graph. If the sine graph is shifted 90° to the left, it overlaps perfectly with the cosine graph. sin θ = cos(θ - 90°) (shift the cosine graph to the right). cos θ = sin(θ + 90°) (shift the sine graph to the left).

claims.claim: The effect of q in y = a cos θ + q is called a vertical shift: the whole cosine graph shifts up or down by q units.
For q > 0, the cosine graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units.
For q < 0, the cosine graph is shifted vertically downwards by q units.
For q = 0, the graph is the basic cosine graph.
The value of a affects the amplitude of the graph, that is, the height of the peaks and the depth of the troughs.
For a > 1, there is a vertical stretch and the amplitude increases.
For a = 1, the graph is the basic cosine graph.
For 0 < a < 1, the amplitude decreases.
For a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis.
For -1 < a < 0, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude decreases.
For a < -1, there is a reflection about the x-axis and the amplitude increases.
Amplitude is always positive.
To discover the effect of q, plot y = cos θ - 2, cos θ - 1, cos θ, cos θ + 1 and cos θ + 2 on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of q.
To discover the effect of a, plot y = -2 cos θ, -cos θ, cos θ and 2 cos θ on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, then use the results to deduce the effect of a.

The cosine values in the table are rounded to 2 decimal places.
Plot the values of θ on the x-axis and cos θ on the y-axis, choosing an appropriate scale.
